findings.problem: BudgetWorkflow uses status: String and separate is_validated/is_sent bools, allowing every combination of invalid states (e.g. is_sent=true with status="draft", both flags false, status="sent" without is_sent=true). The struct has no constructor enforcing lifecycle invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Any code path can construct or mutate a BudgetWorkflow into an inconsistent state, making runtime checks everywhere instead of compile-time guarantees. Callers cannot rely on the type to encode valid lifecycle transitions.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a BudgetStatus enum, replace is_validated and is_sent with a BudgetLifecycle typestate enum or a single state enum combining both dimensions. Remove public fields and provide a fallible constructor or builder that enforces transitions.

findings.problem: id: String is a primitive domain identifier with no domain-specific type. There is no BudgetId newtype enforcing format, uniqueness, or non-empty invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicates, or malformed IDs can flow through the system undetected at the type level. Every caller must re-validate the primitive.
findings.fix: Introduce a `pub struct BudgetId(String)` with a fallible constructor (e.g. `try_from`) that rejects empty/whitespace-only values. Use BudgetId as the field type.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts a BudgetWorkflow and unconditionally sets status="sent", is_sent=true, without checking any preconditions (is_validated, lifecycle state, etc.). It takes ownership but mutates in place then returns, ignoring any prior state.
findings.failure_mode: Any BudgetWorkflow — whether invalid, never validated, or already sent — can be marked sent. This silently corrupts workflow state with no error returned to the caller.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to a fallible function that takes the current state enum (or typestate token) and returns Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError>. The signature should encode the required pre-state as a type parameter or enum variant so only a pre-sent state can transition to sent.

findings.problem: The module mixes data (BudgetWorkflow struct) and behavior (mark_sent) with no functional core / imperative shell boundary. There is no pure core that can be tested in isolation from any side effects.
findings.failure_mode: State transitions cannot be tested as pure deterministic functions. Any change to behavior risks breaking invariants without isolated test coverage.
findings.fix: Extract the transition logic into a pure function `fn transition_to_sent(state: BudgetState) -> Result<BudgetState, BudgetError>` in a dedicated core module. Keep the struct as inert data valid by construction.

findings.problem: All fields on BudgetWorkflow are pub, so any module can set status, is_validated, is_sent, or sent_at_epoch_ms directly without going through a constructor or transition function.
findings.failure_mode: Invariants enforced by constructors or transition functions are trivially bypassed by direct field assignment from any module in the crate.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a sealed constructor and transition methods only.

findings.problem: mark_sent has return type BudgetWorkflow with no Result or error type. Invalid transitions have no way to communicate failure to the caller.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish a successful transition from a silently ignored invalid one. Error handling is impossible at the type level.
findings.fix: Define a `pub enum BudgetError { InvalidTransition, AlreadySent, ... }` and change the return type to `Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError>`.

findings.problem: The struct has is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, and sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> as separate fields. This triad encodes a state machine but the compiler cannot enforce valid combinations.
findings.failure_mode: States like (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) or (is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=None) are representable but semantically invalid. Bugs manifest at runtime, not compile time.
findings.fix: Model the lifecycle as a single enum typestate (e.g. `enum BudgetState { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at: Instant } }`) so only valid states exist.

findings.problem: mark_sent assigns `item.status = "sent".to_string()` — allocates a new String for a constant literal. Status should be an enum variant, not heap-allocated string.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation on every transition. If status remains String, every comparison or match requires allocation or reference coercion.
findings.fix: Use an enum for status and eliminate the String allocation entirely.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any transition function
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns in BudgetWorkflow lifecycle
no allocation audit — no try_reserve or bounded-allocation handling anywhere in the crate
no second-ring evidence (no command, no workload description, no variance data)
no behavioral tests exercising invalid state transitions (e.g. marking non-validated budget as sent)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate's core architecture — primitive-typed data struct with unguarded transitions — makes it fundamentally incompatible with Holzman Rust guarantees. Even if all findings were fixed, no benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation audits exist to verify performance or safety claims.
